text.p: Ford Motor Co. Thursday boosted its quarterly dividend by 9 percent in a move aimed at showing Wall Street its cost-cutting efforts are paying off.
"Today's action reflects continued improvement in our operations that stem directly from higher automotive margins and lower costs," Chairman Alex Trotman said in a statement.

The dividend hike, to 42 cents a share, is the sixth increase since the first quarter of 1994. Ford last raised the amount in third quarter of 1996, when it increased the per-share quarterly payout to 38.5 from 35 cents.

The new amount brings Ford's annual dividend yield to about 5.1 percent, based on Thursday's price of $32.875, which was unchanged from Wednesday. The yield, equal to the annual dividend payout divided by the stock price, is one tool used to measure the return on an investment.
Ford's new annual payout brings it closer to the 5.33 dividend yield that Chrysler Corp. shares currently offer. General Motors Corp.'s common stock has a 3.67 percent yield at Thursday's prices.
Analysts said the dividend action sends the correct signal to investors about the improvements Ford is making in efforts to reduce costs and product development expenditures.
"The bottom line is, it's consistent with the company's operating performance and the expectation of a strong cash flow," said James Irwin, an analyst at Goldman Sachs & Co.

Ford is scheduled to release its first quarter earnings April 16. According to First Call Corp., the consensus analyst estimate for the period is 88 cents a share vs. 53 cents a year ago, when the automaker reported net income of $653 million.
Within the last week, two analysts have boosted their estimates for the first qaurter, while one has lowered their estimate, First Call said.

Nicholas Lobaccaro, an analyst at Bear, Stearns & Co., was one of those more positive on the company. He increased his stock rating to a "buy," citing recent actions Ford has taken to boost its near-term automotive profitability. Last month, the company said it would kill off four slow-selling vehicles by the end of the 1997 model year.

"Under the direction of Alex Trotman and (Ford Automotive President) Jac Nasser, we believe that Ford's top management is focused like a laser on improving near-term automotive profitabilty in all geographic regions," Lobaccaro wrote in a recent report.
The second-quarter dividend is payable June 2 to shareholders of record on May 2.
